stem: The Period 3 elements, Na to S, all react with oxygen to form oxides.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the trend in acid/base behaviour of the oxides of the Period 3 elements, from Na to S.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State and explain the trend, from Na to S, in the maximum oxidation number of the Period 3 elements in their oxides.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Sodium oxide and phosphorus(V) oxide both react with water.

**Name** the product of each reaction.

| reaction | product |
| :--- | :--- |
| sodium oxide with water |  |
| phosphorus(V) oxide with water |  |

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why phosphorus(V) oxide has a low melting point of approximately $300^{\circ}\text{C}$ but magnesium oxide has a high melting point of approximately $2850^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem: Aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, reacts separately with both acids and alkalis.
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of aluminium oxide with excess aqueous hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of aluminium oxide with excess aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Describe the lattice structure of silicon(IV) oxide.

Your answer should include reference to the arrangement of the silicon and oxygen atoms and the bonds between them.

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.stem:
Sodium oxide and silicon(IV) oxide react to form sodium silicate(IV), $\text{Na}_2\text{SiO}_3$.

Sodium oxide is obtained from the thermal decomposition of sodium carbonate.

Write equations for the following reactions:

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text: the thermal decomposition of sodium carbonate, forming sodium oxide and carbon dioxide.
